purpose: The ONE definition of the mutation-class axis. Every consumer (record-schema.json enums, choreo/stats.py, render.py, mlir-shared/lane.py, iree/collect_stats.py, triton/collect.py) derives from this file instead of restating the list. schema/check_class_axis.py fails the build on drift.
_path_classes_note: The pipeline `path_class` field now carries the canonical outcome vocabulary (mutation-specs-v2.md section 9.6.1), not the retired P1-P4 codes. It lists the four outcomes a stated defect can take plus `L`. `unexpressible` is not a path value: a spec the suite cannot state still has a path, and the N/A reason lives in `prohibition`/`admissible`. Legacy mapping: P1->rt-check, P2->avoided, P3->unchecked, P4->ct-check, L->L.

status_meaning.measured: the lane ran the class and has cells for it in S1
status_meaning.n/a: the lane ran the class and its surface cannot express the defect. This is a MEASURED verdict, and it carries a reason. n_na = n_target_per_class.
status_meaning.uncompared: the class is out of scope for this lane, so the lane emits NO cell for it. A missing cell is NOT an n/a cell: `n/a` says the surface was measured and cannot express the defect, while a missing cell says the lane was never run against the class. Conflating them would let a coverage gap read as a capability limit.
status_meaning.not_ready: the lane has published no results/ at all

canonical_stats_key.note: The key the MERGED view (render.py -> stats-merged.json) and the paper tables use. Lane-local stats.json files are not yet uniform -- choreo and triton write S1_detection_matrix because their S1 block is nested under `per_class`, mlir-linalg/mlir-low/iree write S1_detection flat -- and render.py normalizes both into this key. The per-lane spelling is recorded in lanes.<lane>.stats_key so the difference is enumerated and checked rather than accidental. New lanes must write this key.

classes.name: hardware/target constraint
classes.note: Since 2026-09-14 this class ALSO carries the launch-geometry, per-SM-resource and feature-gating limits at M3.17-M3.26. The former standalone `L` class was folded IN here, because a launch/resource/feature limit IS a target constraint. `L` survives only as a path class (attribution-only). See specs/mutation-specs-v2.md 4.

classes.name: iteration-validity
classes.note: M4 is the COST-FILTER CONTROL: it routes the iteration-validity obligation (a zero, negative, runtime-zero or reversed bound; a zero step; an empty iteration space), so it stays OUT of the detection ranking (role: control). M4.4 is a deliberate noop control (excluded from the admissible denominator); counting it as admissible means the oracle regressed. Measured on the three lanes whose programs AUTHOR a loop bound (choreo `parallelby`/`with-in`, triton `range`, mlir-low `affine.for`/`scf.for`). Decision 2026-09-23: linalg and iree are DROPPED from M4 -- a `linalg.generic`'s iteration bound is derived from the operand domain by the compiler, not authored by the program, so the detection families (zero/negative/reversed bound, zero step) have no program value to corrupt; the prohibition is `derived`. They hold M4 at `uncompared` (the lane was never run against it) and emit no cell. M4-g (degenerate pad) is a LIVE family -- its realisations M4.7 `negpad` / M4.8 `emptypad` are `rt-check` -- so the class cell is 7x8=56, not 48. (The 2026-09-23 withdrawal by `prohibition: absent` was reversed 2026-09-24; a new mutation-only kernel may carry the state on a lane whose surface does not author a padded extent.)

not_classes.meaning: launch-status PATH class (attribution-only). Never a mutation class and never enters an admissible denominator. Stored in the `path_class` field, whose enum still admits it.

Proposed `decision reuse` (cache/guard/specialization-key corruption). Ruled NOT APPLICABLE in specs/mutation-specs-v2.md 9.5.3 -- there is no reuse mechanism in the pinned build to corrupt. It is not a mutation class and has no operators.
not_classes.guard: If a reviewer asks for M5, point at 9.5.3; do not add a class.

paper_category.note: The published bug taxonomy. It is NOT the class axis and is NOT injective against it: M1 maps to {oob, stride, wrong-shape}, M2 to {dim-mismatch, wrong-shape}, M3 to {dim-mismatch, stride, hw}, M4 to {stride}. Grouping a table by paper_category merges M1 and M4. Group by `class` when the class is the question.

path_class.note: Check-path classification (specs/mutation-specs-v2.md 9.6). Orthogonal to the class axis: it says whether a defect is assessed, a hard error, unchecked, warning-only, or a launch-status reject.

spec_version.port: raw/e1_mutant_records.json holds v2.1 as of 996087b plus the `applicable` mint in run_e1.py `stamp()`; what remains is collect.py and stats.py over it, which is what carries `applicable` into results/choreo/mutant.jsonl.
spec_version.note: This lane TARGETS v2.1 and holds one on its raw run output. Three files, three honest states. (1) raw/mutant_manifest.json is the PLAN: it carries spec_id, path_class, prohibition and spec_version on all 107 mutants. It does not carry `applicable` because a plan records the in-process Python attribute `admissible` -- and `admissible` is the per-mutant verdict while `spec_admissible` is the spec's. A plan is not a record. (2) raw/e1_mutant_records.json is the RAW run output (run_e1.py). 996087b regenerated it and stamped `spec_version: v2.1`, but run_e1.py's V21_FIELDS stopped at spec_version and never minted `applicable`, so the file held four of the five RECORD fields under a full-port label -- the partial port `corpus.declared-files` rightly rejects. run_e1.py now mints `applicable` in `stamp()` the same way collect.py:296 does (the per-mutant `admissible`, else the spec's), and `--stamp-only` backfilled all 107 rows with zero verdict drift: five of five fields, verified by reading the file rather than by trusting the label. (3) results/choreo/mutant.jsonl is the COLLECTED output and is still v1 -- it holds no spec_version field at all, because it was collected 2026-09-10, one day before the vocabulary landed. The port is therefore done on the raw side and outstanding on the collected side: collect.py and stats.py still have to be re-run before any figure is read from results/choreo/mutant.jsonl at v2.1.

spec_version.port: benchmark2 SOTA spec-v2.1 port -- a spec register plus v2.1 stamping in triton/driver.py, then re-run the lane. Changes no verdict; only what a record can express.
spec_version.note: Collected 2026-09-10, one day before the v2.1 path-class vocabulary landed. The records validate at v1 and cannot be read for the path axis. The release label says which fields a record CAN BE READ FOR; it is not a date. A corpus holding spec_id but none of the other four v2.1 fields is therefore the normal shape of this lane, not a half-finished migration. The corpus now DOES carry `spec_id` on all 29 records, so that the 27 M1 + 2 M3 instances can be attributed to a family (the register ids are the lane's own decided mapping in triton/driver.py). Only the three path fields are missing, which is why the release stays `v1`.

spec_version.note: Collected 2026-09-10, one day before the v2.1 path-class vocabulary landed. The records validate at v1 and cannot be read for the path axis. The release label says which fields a record CAN BE READ FOR; it is not a date. A corpus holding spec_id but none of the other four v2.1 fields is therefore the normal shape of this lane, not a half-finished migration. The attribution extract iree/raw/mutants.jsonl DOES carry `spec_id` on all 64 records, so the M2 mutations can be attributed to a family (the ids are the register ids M2.n). Only the three path fields are missing, which is why the release stays `v1`. The lane also omitted the v1 field `stage`; that was a missing writer line, not a missing measurement. `stage` is a total projection of `outcome` (schema/records.py STAGE_FOR_OUTCOME, 245/245 agreement measured across three lanes), so it was repaired exactly and this lane is now fully v1-conformant.

spec_version.port: CUTLASS/CuTe candidate lane: 15 operators gated against CPU references, a launch-time M4/L battery, a compile-only M3 probe battery and a one-per-family M1 probe slice, all emitted as v2.1 mutant records (cutlass/mutrec.py). It is not covered by the v2.1 port (no family manifests, M2 uncompared) until a promotable corpus and a conforming S1 block exist.
spec_version.note: CUTLASS/CuTe lane, PROMOTED on the sm_86 dev host: 15 operators gated against CPU references plus a launch-time M4/L battery and compile-only M3/M1 probe batteries, all emitted as v2.1 mutant records by cutlass/mutrec.py. M1/M3/M4 are `measured`; M2 (shape contract) is `uncompared` -- the CuTe surface can express it, so it is NOT `n/a`; it is out of this lane's remit and carries no S1 cell (declared in `S1_declared_uncompared`). The M1 cell is a ONE-PER-FAMILY PROBE SLICE (M1-a..M1-h) and is COMPILE-ONLY: a hand-written CuTe kernel owns its own index arithmetic, so 7 families are `unchecked` and only M1-g (index >= rank) is statically detained. The M3 outcomes are COMPILE-ONLY too (sm_90a TMA/GMMA probes were compiled, not run, on sm_86); the manifest pin is 2xH800 sm_120, so an sm_120 re-run is pending and the lane keeps `complete: false` in its own stats.

triton.M2: no cross-tensor shape contract on the Triton surface: extents are the programmer's problem, so a rank/extent disagreement is not expressible (mutation-specs-v2.md 5)

mlir-linalg.M1: no element-access defect is expressible on the tensor/linalg entry surface: there are no addressable memory locations before lowering (mutation-specs-v2.md 5)
mlir-linalg.M3: hardware-constraint defects need a device target; this lane is a CPU JIT with no hardware contract to violate (mutation-specs-v2.md 5, measured)

mlir-low.M2: no cross-tensor shape contract exists on the memref/affine surface: shapes are already concrete buffer descriptors, so a rank/extent disagreement is not expressible (mutation-specs-v2.md 5)
mlir-low.M3: hardware-constraint defects have no expressible form on the plain memref/affine kernel surface: it authors no mma/tma/alignment construct, and lowering it to a device launch does not add one; launch-geometry (M3.17-M3.26) is outside this lane's M1 mandate (mutation-specs-v2.md 5, measured)

iree.M1: no interior access at the IREE entry surface: a mutant has no expressible form because the shape is the only thing the entry check can see (mutation-specs-v2.md 5)
iree.M3: no mma/tma/alignment construct on the IREE entry surface (mutation-specs-v2.md 5)

uncompared_key.note: Every lane writes this key alongside its S1 block, listing the classes it was never run against, so a class missing from S1 is a STATED scope decision rather than a missing loop iteration. An empty object means the lane has no uncompared class. schema/check_class_axis.py asserts classes[] equals the axis's uncompared set for that lane.

uncompared_reason: A class this lane was never run against. It emits NO cell -- a missing cell is not an `n/a` cell (`n/a` is a measured verdict), so the two must never read alike. M4 is `uncompared` on mlir-linalg and iree since 2026-09-23 (decision: dropped, not measured -- a `linalg.generic` iteration bound is compiler-derived from the operand domain, so the program authors no bound to corrupt; the prohibition is `derived`). It is measured on the program-authored-loop lanes choreo, triton and mlir-low. See schema/class-axis.json `status_meaning` and render.py.
NON_ADDITIVE_v1_1: v1.1 frozen records with class == "L" must be remapped to "M3" (M3.17-M3.26). The committed E1 baseline (results/choreo/mutant.jsonl, 120 records) is M1/M2/M3 only and needs no remap.
